#!/bin/bash
# Testcontainers speaks the Docker API at the node's /var/run/docker.sock. That socket is held by the node's engine proxy, which forwards it to /run/docker.raw.sock and answers
# "502 Bad response from Docker engine" while nothing listens there. The node has only containerd (a gRPC socket): no Docker engine. Give the node one: run dockerd in the node
# ON TOP OF the node's containerd (--containerd) and let it listen where the proxy forwards to, detached so that it outlives this script. The proxy and containerd stay as they are.
set -e
W=/tmp/bench76980610
NR="$W/bin/node-run"
"$NR" test -S /run/containerd/containerd.sock
"$NR" sh -c 'setsid -f dockerd --containerd /run/containerd/containerd.sock --host unix:///run/docker.raw.sock --pidfile /run/dockerd.pid >/tmp/bench76980610/dockerd.log 2>&1 </dev/null'
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do "$NR" docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock version >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
"$NR" docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock version --format 'docker server {{.Server.Version}}'
"$W/bin/run-test"

#!/bin/bash
# dockerd on a socket of its own; Testcontainers is told where it is through the job's HOME (the proxy keeps docker.sock)
#!/bin/bash
set -e
W=/tmp/bench76980610
NR="$W/bin/node-run"
"$NR" sh -c 'setsid -f dockerd --containerd /run/containerd/containerd.sock --host unix:///run/ci-docker.sock --pidfile /run/dockerd.pid >/tmp/bench76980610/dockerd.log 2>&1 </dev/null'
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do "$NR" docker -H unix:///run/ci-docker.sock version >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
echo "docker.host=unix:///run/ci-docker.sock" > "$W/home/.testcontainers.properties"
"$W/bin/run-test"

#!/bin/bash
# a Docker daemon of its own on the host side (its own containerd, its own data), reached through a socket in the shared /tmp
#!/bin/bash
set -e
W=/tmp/bench76980610
NR="$W/bin/node-run"
H=$W/hostdocker; mkdir -p "$H"
sudo setsid -f dockerd --data-root "$H/data" --exec-root "$H/exec" --pidfile "$H/dockerd.pid" --host unix://$H/docker.sock --bridge none --iptables=false >"$H/dockerd.log" 2>&1 </dev/null
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do sudo docker -H unix://$H/docker.sock version >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
echo "docker.host=unix://$H/docker.sock" > "$W/home/.testcontainers.properties"
"$W/bin/run-test"

for _ in $(seq 1 60); do "$NR" docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock version >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done

#!/bin/bash
# replace the proxy by a stand-in that answers the first requests of Testcontainers (ping, version, info) with fixed JSON
#!/bin/bash
set -e
W=/tmp/bench76980610
NR="$W/bin/node-run"
cat > "$W/fake_docker.py" <<'EOF'
import http.server, json, os, socketserver
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        body = b"OK" if self.path.endswith("/_ping") else json.dumps({"ServerVersion": "27.0.0", "ApiVersion": "1.46", "OperatingSystem": "fake", "Name": "fake"}).encode()
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body))); self.send_header("Api-Version", "1.46"); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(body)
    do_POST = do_GET
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
class S(socketserver.UnixStreamServer):
    def get_request(self):
        r, _ = super().get_request(); return r, ("fake", 0)
os.path.exists("/var/run/docker.sock") and os.unlink("/var/run/docker.sock")
S("/var/run/docker.sock", H).serve_forever()
EOF
"$NR" pkill -f engine-proxy.py
"$NR" sh -c 'setsid -f python3 /tmp/bench76980610/fake_docker.py >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null'
sleep 2
"$W/bin/run-test" || true
